rail.title: Apps
rail.emptyHint: Play sound in an app, then refresh
rail.alsoHint: Apply the same change to this app
rail.stopRoute: Stop output and return to the system default
rail.stopAllConfirm: Click again to return everything to the system default

sourceLevel.valueLabel: Level this app gives the audio of {{process}}, in percent
sourceLevel.hint: Gain this app applies to this program's audio on its way to the devices it is duplicated to, as a percentage: 100 leaves it as produced, below attenuates, above amplifies. Like the device volume and the delay, it acts on the duplicated copies only — the device Windows plays directly is not affected. Drag sideways, or scroll / use the arrow keys for {{step}}% at a time (hold Shift for ×10); click to type an exact value

deviceLatency.reading: Measured here: {{ms}} ms. Covers the software side only — what a codec or a Bluetooth link adds on top cannot be observed from user mode

deviceVolume.valueLabel: Volume of {{device}}, relative to the loudest device, in percent

primaryVolume.hint: Primary volume: this is the program's own session volume, so only the main path gets quieter — the engine compensates the copies, and they are unaffected. It stops at 5%; to silence the main device while the copies keep playing, make another device the main output and turn this one down as a copy

stage.guide: Select an app on the left
stage.primaryTitle: The main device is played by Windows itself, so software delay has nothing to hold back — that is why there is no delay row here. Volume works through the program's own session volume: only the main path gets quieter, and the copies are compensated so they are unaffected
stage.promoteTitle: Make this the device the system plays directly; the others become copies of it
stage.promoteBlockedTitle: Its delay compensation is larger than the Main device's, and the system plays that one directly — software delay can only hold sound back, so this device can only align as a copy
stage.addTargetTitle: Play through another device, or send the sound into another program's input
stage.feedTitleLive: {{name}}'s input receives this program's audio through the configured carrier
stage.feedTitleSuspended: Recorded but not moving: {{source}} is routed to a device, and the per-app output slot belongs to it. Stop that route and the feed resumes on its own
stage.feedTitleNoCarrier: Recorded but not moving: no carrier is configured — pick a loopback pair in Settings → Feed carrier
stage.removeFeed: Stop sending this program's audio into {{name}}'s input
stage.feederTitle: Click to open this program's own board
stage.stripPrimaryNote: This is the program's session volume — only the main path changes; the copies are compensated.
stage.stripPrimaryLatency: The primary is played by Windows directly, so there is no measured latency to show here.
stage.inspectorHint: Click a card's number to tune it — the program itself, a device's delay and volume. The dashed card adds a destination.
stage.inspectorHubNoRoute: Not routed — pick destination cards to build a plan, then click the program card to apply it.

briefing.tooltip: Let me tell you where things stand — plainly, simply, no beating around the bush.
briefing.title: Where things stand
briefing.empty: Nothing is redirected: every app follows the system default device, {{device}}.
briefing.emptyNoDevice: Nothing is redirected: every app follows the system default device.
briefing.routeOne: {{process}} plays from {{device}} now, and follows nothing else.
briefing.staged: The board still has changes waiting — click the program card to make them real.
briefing.feedLine: {{process}} is sending its audio into {{targets}}' input.
briefing.feedHeldLine: {{process}} has a feed into {{targets}}, held while it plays through a device.

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoRememberDesc: Remember each program's device routing and restore it automatically
settings.resetEndpointsDesc: Releases a program that no longer follows the system's playback device; routed programs are left alone
settings.stopAllRoutesDesc: Returns every routed program to the system default at once. The programs a route is not using are left alone.
settings.closeToTrayDesc: When on, closing hides the window to the tray while routes keep running; when off, closing quits the app and stops them
settings.autostartDesc: Launches silently into the tray at sign-in; remembered routes are ready before you open anything
settings.delayNote: Delay is set per device: here, on the settings rows, or in the tuning strip of a copy selected on the routing board. It applies only when one program goes to several devices — a single-device route is played by the system directly.
settings.calibrationNote: The measured latency covers the software side only; what a Bluetooth link itself adds cannot be measured here, so align by ear.
settings.delayRangeDesc: Delays can be set within this ± range
settings.delayStepDesc: How much each − / + click changes; an exact value can also be typed
settings.sourceLevelsAlignDesc: Brings every duplicating program that is playing up to the loudest one's level
settings.sourceLevelsNote: A program playing through several devices wears its level as the dial under its card on the routing board. The level is the gain this app applies to its own copy of that sound — the program's own volume and anything Windows stores are untouched. 100 leaves it as produced, and it acts on the copies only.
settings.feedCarrierDesc: Sending one program's audio into another's input runs it through a loopback pair: the source plays into the pair's playback side, and the target records from its recording side. Pick the pair a loopback driver provides (such as VB-Cable); without one, feeds are remembered but stay silent.
settings.feedCarrierRenderHint: The pair's playback endpoint — often named “… Input”
settings.feedCarrierCaptureHint: The pair's recording endpoint — often named “… Output”
settings.feedCarrierDetected: Found {{driver}} — both sides are on the lists
settings.feedCarrierMissing: No loopback driver found. A free one is enough — install VB-Cable and the lists here refresh on their own, no restart needed.
settings.aboutDesc: Per-app audio routing for Windows — Rust talking to Windows Core Audio directly, no third-party executables.

startup.upgradeTitle: An earlier version ran on this PC
startup.upgradeBody: It may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you encounter this, clear it with the button below; otherwise no action is needed.
startup.upgradeBodyVersion: The last version to run on this PC was {{version}}, and it may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you encounter this, clear it with the button below; otherwise no action is needed.
startup.resetHint: This clears every program that is running now, including a device you set by hand in the volume mixer. A program that is not running keeps its device until it starts.
startup.resetDone: Cleared the fixed output device of {{n}} program(s).
startup.resetRemaining: {{processes}} could not be cleared — a program must be playing audio to be released; try again.

wizard.welcomeBody: This is a per-app audio router: each program's sound goes where you send it, while everything else keeps following the system default. Windows cannot do this on its own — that is the whole point of the app.
wizard.welcomePoint1: Route any program to any output device — or to several at once
wizard.welcomePoint2: Feed one program's audio into another program's microphone input
wizard.welcomePoint3: Everything is remembered: routes and feeds come back with the program
wizard.boardBody: The program you select sits in the middle. Its destinations line up on the right — output devices first, then programs receiving its sound. A line from the program to a destination is the route itself, and the number on a card is its place in that order.
wizard.boardPoint1: Click a destination card to connect it or let it go
wizard.boardPoint2: Nothing changes until you click the program card — the board proposes first, applies on your word
wizard.boardPoint3: The dock under the board holds delay and volume for each destination
wizard.carrierBody: Sending sound into a program's microphone runs through a loopback driver's endpoint pair. The app ships no driver — one you already have is recognized here, and the free VB-Cable is one click away. Skipping this costs nothing else: routing to devices works without it.
wizard.carrierMissing: No loopback driver found. Install the free VB-Cable now, or pick the pair later in Settings → Feed carrier.
wizard.backgroundBody: The app lives in the tray and keeps routes working with the window closed. Two habits to choose:
wizard.backgroundAutostartHint: Starts hidden in the tray, so remembered routes are already in place when you sign in.
wizard.backgroundCloseToTray: Closing the window only tucks it away
wizard.backgroundCloseToTrayHint: Otherwise the X exits the app and stops every route.
